authoredPrompt: This figure is a single Cartesian graph showing a rational function together with the two asymptotes it approaches. The horizontal x-axis carries integer ticks from -5 to 5, the vertical y-axis carries even ticks from -12 to 12, and both are tipped with arrowheads. A dashed orange vertical line stands at x = 1 and runs the full height of the frame, labeled x = 1 in orange near its lower end. A dashed teal line of steep positive slope crosses from the lower left to the upper right, labeled Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 above and right of the origin. The function is a solid dark blue curve in two branches. The left branch enters at the lower left pressed against the teal line, rises to a shallow turning point just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunges off the bottom of the frame as it nears the orange line. The right branch descends from the top just right of x = 1, turns at a minimum near y = 9, and climbs away to the upper right, again closing on the teal line. Drawing the curve and both dashed lines on one set of axes lets the reader compare each branch against the boundary it hugs. The graph illustrates the case in which the numerator exceeds the denominator in degree by one, so the polynomial quotient supplies a slanted rather than horizontal end behavior.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for an x-value probe: the learner drags x along either branch, a point moves on the rational curve, and guide distances to x = 1 and y = 3x + 1 show why the vertical asymptote controls local blow-up while the slant asymptote controls end behavior.
- Toggle between curve-only, asymptotes-only, and combined views: the dashed vertical and slanted lines appear or disappear over the same axes, making clear that the curve can approach two different kinds of boundary without either dashed line being part of the function.
authoredContext:
To find the equation of the slant asymptote, divide 3 x 2 −2x+1 x−1. The quotient is 3x+1, and the remainder is 2. The slant asymptote is the graph of the line g(x)=3x+1. See the figure.

Slant Asymptote when f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0 where degree of p>degree of qby1.

Graph of f(x)=(3x^2-2x+1)/(x-1) with its vertical asymptote at x=1 and a slant asymptote aty=3x+1.

Case 3: If the degree of the denominator = degree of the numerator, there is a horizontal asymptote at y= a n b n, where a n and b n are the leading coefficients of p(x) and q(x) for f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0.
